item.title: Aceh’s Bitter Lesson, Relearned
item.description: In 2004, Aceh was hardest hit by the Indian Ocean tsunami. In 2025, Indonesia’s most disaster-aware province was among the worst hit by floods.

item.title: What is Happening to North Korea’s Jangmadang Free Markets?
item.description: Will the Kim regime be successful in uprooting this core element of North Korea’s black market economy?

item.title: The Bondi Attack, the Islamic State, and the Price of Strategic Shortsightedness
item.description: The shooters’ actual connections to Islamic State groups in the Philippines may be tenuous, but the spotlight provides an opportunity to reflect on the group’s persistence and the importance of the ongoing Bangsamoro peace process.

item.title: Invoking History: Xi Jinping’s Challenge to Okinawan Sovereignty and the US-Japan Alliance
item.description: Xi’s invocation of tributary history is less a claim over sovereignty than it is an attack on the U.S.-Japan alliance.

item.title: Cambodia Counts the Costs of Its Border Conflict with Thailand
item.description: 424 Cambodian troops have been wounded and 13 killed in one province alone since the outbreak of fighting on December 7.

item.title: Thai Prosecutors Urged to Drop Malaysian Defamation Case Against Australian Journalist
item.description: Murray Hunter was expected to appear before a court in mid-December following his indictment but his trial was postponed. Instead he attended a four-hour Senate Committee hearing into enhancing anti-SLAPP legislation.

item.title: The World Is Failing Cambodia (Again) – and This Time Everyone Is Suffering
item.description: Western strategic dissonance, U.N. cowardice, a gutted civil society, and cynical Thai aggression are providing cover for a weakened Hun Sen.

item.title: 2025: The Year Pakistan Stepped Back into the Spotlight
item.description: After years of relative marginalization in global affairs, Pakistan was able to reclaim a prominent position on the world stage.

item.title: The Return of Factional Conflict in South Korea’s Foreign Policy
item.description: Interministerial discord made a recent comeback, pitting the so-called “self-reliance faction” against the “pro-alliance faction” over how best to approach North Korea.

item.title: Has Nepal’s Second Biggest Party Just Committed Political Harakiri?
item.description: By electing the highly unpopular and recently ousted PM Oli as party chief, the CPN-UML has thumbed its nose at the Gen Z demand for fresh and young leaders.
